documents.service_pressure_basis: corrected mean case mouth pressure plus 3 standard deviations, ammunition conditioned at +21 C (Chapter 2 para 1a and Annex B sheet 1)
documents.note: Genuine NATO AOP-4172 Edition A Version 1, September 2020. The held file is a secondary mirror copy from jedi-sec.us. No archived copy was found on the NATO public release host. The document states ammunition acceptance limits. It does not state a weapon proof pressure. It refers to AEP-97 Volumes 12 and 13. It also states a corrected mean case mouth pressure not exceeding 455 MPa at +52 C and -54 C. It states a port pressure minus 3 SD not less than 103 MPa at +21 C. It states a velocity variation of +50/-80 m/s from the +21 C sample at +52 C and -54 C. Absolute velocity is not stated.

documents.service_pressure_basis: maximum corrected mean case mouth pressure plus 3 standard deviations for the +21 C sample (Volume 12 para 12.2.2 table)
documents.note: NATO AEP-97 Edition A Version 1, October 2020, Volume 12. This volume holds the Combination Electronic Pressure Velocity and Action Time (EPVAT) Test Procedures. The held file is the primary copy from the NATO public release server at diweb.hq.nato.int. The Internet Archive supplied the copy. Port pressure minus 3 SD is not less than 103 MPa at +21 C. Velocity variation is +50/-80 m/s from the +21 C sample at +52 C and -54 C. The document states no absolute velocity requirement and no weapon proof pressure.

documents.service_pressure_basis: derived as proof pressure divided by 1.25. Para 8.2.2 defines service pressure Pmax as the mean pressure of the service cartridge at 21 C. It defines the proof round as 25 percent in excess. The value 430 MPa is not printed in the table.
documents.note: UK MOD national standard, Proof of Ordnance Munitions Armour and Explosives, Part 1 Requirements. Issue 1 is dated 20 May 2005. The standard was reprinted 24 November 2006 with Amendment 1. Table 2 Corrected Proof Pressure Requirement gives 5375 bar, equal to 537.5 MPa. The pressure is recorded in a NATO design EPVAT barrel with a Kistler 6215 transducer. The alternative is equipment to CIP requirements. The weapon and ammunition are conditioned at 21 C. The held file comes from the UK MOD web archive. NATO EPVAT descriptions cite this standard as the source of the proof pressure.
